items.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002
items.q: But I think what changed me to saxophone was hearing the record “Swiss Movement,” Les McCann and Eddie Harris.

ctx.x: What brought you to the saxophone? Was it your first instrument?

Yeah. Formally anyway. I really wanted to be a drummer, before the age of twelve. But I think what changed me to saxophone was hearing the record “Swiss Movement,” Les McCann and Eddie Harris. Because that was a big hit around 1969, 1970, and that was one of the records my father had and I gravitated toward that. And then with allowance money I started going out and buying a couple of Eddie Harris records and of course Cannonball Adderley’s “Country Preacher” was a big hit at the time. So all of those things, I…
Yeah. We’re going to talk about those guys in a while actually.
